At least three bodies have been recovered the site of a residential building that was hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Services said.

A woman in her forties and a teenage boy have so far been identified as rescue workers continue to search the rubble for those who are still trapped.

Continued warnings of further drone threats near the site are hampering efforts, the service added, but some people were successfully evacuated earlier in the day.

\"We are living a nightmare... only God knows when it will end,\" one woman told the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, who's reporting from Ukraine's Kyiv region.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky following continued Russian attacks on Ukraine on Friday evening and overnight.

Zelensky has justified Ukraine's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, describing it as a \"fair response\" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

He rejected a claim from Russia that the bridge, which links Russia to the peninsular it illegally annexed from Ukraine, was \"exclusively civilian\" in use.

Streeting and Zelensky hugged upon meeting and the British defence secretary explained he had come to Kyiv to see what support Ukraine needs for winter.

The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from Kyiv.

The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially come to an end after countries failed to come to a consensus on a new deal.

The European Union and some other countries rejected a fourth draft agreement over its failure to mention a need to phase out fossil fuels, the largest driver of global climate change.

An EU representative accuses some oil states of hijacking talks, as Russia defends opposing the inclusion of such a commitment and levels direct criticism at the EU in its speech.

The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.

BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard reports from Antalya, in Turkey.

A recording of sex noises appeared to be playing from the audience during the filming of Strictly Come Dancing in Blackpool on Saturday.

Judge Motsi Mabuse was giving feedback to Delta Goodrem when she paused after the sound started playing.

At the end of the programme, presenter Emma Willis apologised to viewers \"if you heard any audio disruptions\".

A BBC spokesperson also issued an apology and said it was \"investigating how this happened\".

BBC journalist Simon Jones has this report.

Read more about the incident during Strictly Come Dancing in Blackpool.

The United Kingdom and European Union reached a deal on Friday strengthening post-Brexit ties following a summit in Brussels.

The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it was a \"good day\" for Britain and Europe, while European Council President António Costa said the EU remains \"open to have the closest possible relationship\" with the UK.

The BBC's political editor Chris Mason and Europe editor Katya Adler analyse the new agreement and what it could mean for future relations between the UK and EU.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal \"isn't fair\" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a \"betrayal of the British people\".

Protests took place across European cities on Friday as marches were held over the cost of living and other issues, including housing shortages and underfunding in education.

Demonstrations took place in Germany, France, Croatia, Italy, the United Kingdom and elsewhere, attracting a lot of young adults.

The BBC's Europe correspondent, Nick Beake, has been reporting from Rome, where thousands of people took part in a march organised by Italy's main trade union.

BBC News Mundo’s Rafael Rojas visits the real-life Miami locations that inspired Vice City, GTA 6’s fictionalised setting, and speaks to locals about the hype surrounding the game.

GTA 6 is set to become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever, with fans booking time off work, and schools warning students not to skip class.

Read more here about how some police departments across the US are warning fans about taking the game to their real lives.

A woman who was drugged by her husband and secretly advertised for sex on the internet has said if people \"recognised their own experience\" after this trial, \"you're not alone and there are people who will believe you\".

Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, spoke outside of Winchester Court and encouraged people to speak out against violence against women and girls.

Four men have been found guilty of sexually abusing Young in the first trial of its kind in the UK.

Philip Young, 50, already pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and raping his wife over a 13-year period at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire.

Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, were found guilty of multiple sexual offences by a jury at Winchester Crown Court. Wilkins and Macksoni were each found guilty of one count of rape.

You can read Joanne Young's statement in full here.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.

Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ).

The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court.

The court found on Thursday that \"genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence\" it had seen.

The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.

The BBC's Anna Holligan is in the Hague and reports on what the ICJ's ruling means.
